thoughts.idea: The strongest understanding is the one you can explain plainly and then test.
thoughts.prompt: Explain a technical idea in three sentences. Where could your explanation fail?

thoughts.idea: Make the claim precise enough that evidence might prove it wrong.
thoughts.prompt: What observation would force you to abandon your favorite hypothesis?

thoughts.idea: In a distributed system, an apparently simple event can have a complicated order.

thoughts.idea: Persistent experiments matter more than a dramatic first guess.

thoughts.idea: Education can give people the ability to challenge inherited assumptions.

thoughts.idea: Unexpected patterns are invitations to seek a proof, not substitutes for one.

nobel.heading: A telescope made from Antarctic ice
nobel.education: Earned a master's degree and a PhD at the University of Louvain (now KU Leuven), Belgium.
nobel.story: He helped pursue an unlikely idea: the clear ice deep below the South Pole might detect particles arriving from distant space. A vast instrument became a new way to study the universe.
nobel.lesson: Start by testing whether an unusual material or environment can become a scientific instrument.

nobel.heading: Why do molecules have a preferred handedness?
nobel.education: Kenso Soai completed chemistry degrees at the University of Tokyo, earning his doctorate in 1979. This education note is about Soai, not Kagan.
nobel.story: Their work explored how chemical reactions favor one mirror-image form of a molecule. Soai's research on self-amplifying reactions offers an especially striking example of how a small difference can grow.
nobel.lesson: Small asymmetries can have large effects. Ask what mechanism amplifies them.

nobel.people: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann & Georg Nagel
nobel.heading: A way to ask neurons questions using light
nobel.education: Karl Deisseroth studied biochemical sciences at Harvard and earned a neuroscience PhD and medical degree at Stanford. This education note is about Deisseroth, not his co-laureates.
nobel.story: Research on light-sensitive proteins helped scientists develop optogenetics. With it, they could study the roles of particular nerve cells by controlling their activity with light.
nobel.lesson: A basic discovery in one organism can help create powerful tools in another field.
nobel.award: 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
